index.metaTitle: AudioProctor — Audio and text accommodation for assessments
index.metaDescription: A Chrome extension and teacher dashboard that delivers audio and text accommodation for assessed students on managed Chromebooks. Built for schools.

hero.headline: Audio and text accommodation for assessments.
hero.subtitle: A Chrome extension and teacher dashboard that delivers audio and text support for assessed students on managed Chromebooks, without storing any student data.

howItWorks.label: How it works
howItWorks.headline: Three steps. No IT ticket required.
howItWorks.step1Body: Sign in with your school Google account, upload an audio file or paste assessment text, and get a short access code and exit word. Takes under a minute.
howItWorks.step2Body: The student types the access code into the AudioProctor extension on their Chromebook. A locked fullscreen player opens for audio, or a read-aloud text reader for text assessments.
howItWorks.step3Body: When the assessment is done, the teacher reads the exit word aloud. The student types it in, the player closes, and the Chromebook returns to normal.

why.label: Why AudioProctor
why.headline: Designed around a real gap in how assessments work.
why.feature1Body: Students are anonymous to the system. No names, no student IDs, no device identifiers. This isn’t just a policy. It’s structural. There’s no place in the database to store student information.
why.feature2Body: Teachers install the extension once from the Chrome Web Store. Students just enter a code — no setup, no configuration, no permissions to manage.
why.feature3Title: Built for how assessments actually work
why.feature3Body: Supports both audio and text-based accommodations in a single tool. The access code model, the lockdown player, and the exit word were all designed around the real friction of delivering accommodations in the classroom.

about.metaDescription: AudioProctor was built by an IT administrator at an Alberta school division who ran into this problem and couldn’t find a solution that didn’t create new privacy issues.
about.pageTitle: Built by someone in the room.
about.problemBody1: When a student requires audio or text accommodation during an assessment, the expectation is clear, but the tools rarely are. Teachers are expected to deliver audio support or provide a text-to-speech reader for students with IEPs or designations, and the standard assessment environment gives them almost nothing to do it with.
about.problemBody2: The workarounds are familiar: another adult in the room reading aloud, screen readers that weren’t calibrated for assessment content, or aging playback hardware that may or may not still work. None of these are consistent. None of them scale. And none of them are what the accommodation is supposed to look like.
about.problemBody3: The friction is structural. Schools have moved to managed Chromebooks and browser-based assessment delivery, but accommodation tooling hasn’t kept pace. The gap isn’t theoretical. It shows up every time a teacher has to improvise a solution five minutes before a test begins.
about.solutionBody1: AudioProctor was built to fill that gap. A teacher uploads an audio file or pastes assessment text, generates a short access code, and hands it to the student. The student enters the code in a Chrome extension on their Chromebook. For audio, a locked fullscreen player opens. The student listens and replays as needed. For text, a fullscreen reader appears with built-in read-aloud powered by the device’s text-to-speech. When the assessment is done, the teacher provides an exit word to close the session.
about.solutionBody2: No student accounts. No student data. No IT ticket per assessment. The extension is deployed once by IT through Google Admin Console and works across every Chromebook in the division from that point forward.
about.pricingBody: AudioProctor is priced by the scope of the purchase. A teacher can sign up free. A school can buy a plan from their minibudget. A division can sign one contract that covers every school, every teacher, and every Chromebook. The price scales with how much of the organization is covered, not with how many features are unlocked.
about.teamTitle: Built by someone in the room
about.teamBody1: AudioProctor was built by an IT administrator at a real Alberta school division who ran into this problem and couldn’t find a solution that didn’t create new privacy risks or require significant infrastructure. The tool reflects what actually happens in schools: how assessments get run, how teachers operate under time pressure, and what IT departments will and won’t support.

privacy.legalNote: ⚠️ IMPORTANT: This is a machine translation of a legal document. Professional human translation review is required before production use.

sections.whatWeCollectBody1: AudioProctor collects two categories of data: teacher account information and anonymous session analytics.
sections.whatWeCollectBody2: Teacher account information: your email address when you sign in with Google, and the display name and school or division name you choose to provide. This information is associated with your account and your uploaded audio files.
sections.whatWeCollectBody3: Anonymous session analytics: when a student uses an access code to play an audio assessment, AudioProctor records a log of playback events for that session. These events include: code entered, playback started, playback paused, playback resumed, playback completed, audio replayed, exit word used, and session expired. Each event records its type, the time it occurred, and, for pause and replay events, the position in the audio (in seconds). No student identity is attached to any event at any level.
sections.noStudentDataTitle: What we do not collect about students
sections.noStudentDataBody: Students using AudioProctor are anonymous to the system. We do not collect student names, student IDs, Alberta Student Numbers (ASNs), device identifiers, IP addresses, or any information that could identify an individual student. Session events cannot be linked to a specific student. They record only that an event occurred, not who caused it. The same access code can be used by multiple students; AudioProctor does not distinguish between them.
sections.teacherDataBody: Your email address is used solely to associate your uploaded audio files and session analytics with your account. It is not shared with third parties, not used for marketing, and not sold. Session analytics, visible to you through the teacher dashboard, are also available in aggregate form to your school or division administrator if your account is attached to one. Division administrators see only school-level totals; they cannot view individual session events.
sections.storageBody: Audio files, account data, and session analytics are stored with Supabase on infrastructure located in North America. All data in transit is encrypted via TLS. Audio files are stored in private buckets and are never publicly accessible.
sections.retentionBody: Audio files expire automatically based on the expiry window set at upload and are deleted at that time. Session analytics associated with an audio file are deleted when that file is deleted. If you delete your account, all audio files, session analytics, and account data are deleted immediately and permanently. You may delete your account at any time from the Settings page.
sections.thirdPartyBody: AudioProctor uses Google OAuth for authentication. Google’s privacy policy governs that interaction. We do not use third-party advertising networks. Vercel hosts the application infrastructure; Supabase stores data; Resend delivers transactional emails.
sections.foipaBody: AudioProctor is designed for use in Alberta school divisions subject to the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FOIPPA) and the Access to Information Act (ATIA). No student personal information is collected or stored. The anonymous session analytics described above do not constitute personal information as defined under FOIPPA because they cannot be used, alone or in combination with other information held by AudioProctor, to identify a specific individual. Teacher email addresses are processed under the authority of the school division’s existing Google Workspace agreement. Divisions with specific data governance requirements are invited to contact us to discuss a data processing agreement.

sections.acceptanceBody: By creating an account and using AudioProctor, you agree to these terms. If you are accepting on behalf of a school or division, you represent that you have authority to bind that organization.
sections.useOfServiceBody1: AudioProctor is intended for use by educators at accredited schools and school divisions. You are responsible for ensuring that audio files you upload are used in accordance with your division’s assessment policies and any applicable provincial guidelines.
sections.useOfServiceBody2: You may only upload audio content that you have the right to use. Do not upload copyrighted content without appropriate authorization. Provincial assessment audio provided through official channels for accommodation purposes is permissible.
sections.studentPrivacyBody: You agree not to use AudioProctor in any way that would require the collection of student personal information. The service is designed to operate without student data. Preserve that by not including student names, ASN numbers, or other identifiers in filenames, upload labels, or messages.
sections.accountTerminationBody: We reserve the right to suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms, are used in a manner inconsistent with the service’s educational purpose, or represent a security or privacy risk.
sections.limitationBody: AudioProctor is provided as-is. We are not liable for assessment outcomes, data loss due to expiry or deletion, or interruptions to service. For time-sensitive assessments, upload files with sufficient lead time before the assessment window.
sections.changesBody: We may update these terms. Continued use of the service after changes are posted constitutes acceptance. We will notify account holders of material changes by email.

useCases.metaDescription: How schools use AudioProctor to deliver audio and text accommodation during assessments.
useCases.intro: AudioProctor is for any assessed student who needs audio or text support: students with reading disabilities, English Language Learners in applicable assessments, and students with IEPs or designations requiring an accommodation.

cards.provincialBody: A student has a designation requiring audio or text support during provincial assessments. The teacher uploads the official audio track, records their own read-aloud, or pastes the assessment text directly. The student uses the extension during the exam on their managed Chromebook: a locked player for audio, or a fullscreen reader with built-in read-aloud for text.
cards.smallSchoolBody: Schools with only a few accommodation students don’t need a full assistive tech platform. One teacher, one assessment (audio or text), one code. There’s no provisioning, no student accounts, and no coordination with IT for each assessment.
cards.smallSchoolNote: Free tier covers it. No infrastructure required.
cards.divisionRolloutTitle: IT deploys once, every school has it
cards.divisionRolloutBody: IT adds the AudioProctor extension to the Google Admin Console policy. Every managed Chromebook in the division gets it automatically on next sign-in. No teacher installation, no help desk tickets, no version mismatch across schools.
cards.divisionRolloutNote: Division tier: IT deploys once, every school has it.

faq.label: Common Questions
faq.headline: Things divisions ask before signing.
faq.q1: Does this work on any Chromebook?
faq.a1: Yes. AudioProctor works on any Chromebook running Chrome OS. For managed devices, IT can force-install the extension through Google Admin Console so teachers don’t need to do anything. Unmanaged Chromebooks can also install it manually from the Chrome Web Store.
faq.a2: No. Students never sign in. They enter a short access code, given verbally by the teacher, and the extension opens directly to the assessment. There is no student-facing login, no email required, and no account creation.
faq.a3: Only the teacher who created the assessment. Audio files are stored in a private storage bucket; text assessments are stored in the database. Access is controlled by row-level security tied to the teacher’s Google account.
faq.q4: What happens when the access code expires?
faq.a4: Assessments and codes expire automatically after 7 days by default (the division tier allows custom expiry windows). When an assessment expires, the access code stops working and the content is deleted. Teachers can also delete assessments manually at any time from the dashboard.
faq.q5: What’s the difference between audio and text assessments?
faq.a5: Audio assessments play a locked fullscreen audio player. The student listens to the recording. Text assessments display the passage in a fullscreen reader with built-in read-aloud powered by the device’s text-to-speech. Both use the same access code and exit word flow.
faq.q6: Is this compliant with privacy legislation?
faq.a6: AudioProctor does not trigger a Privacy Impact Assessment under Alberta’s Access to Information Act (ATIA). No student personal information is collected or stored at any point. Students are completely anonymous to the system. The only personal data processed is teacher email addresses, which are already covered by existing Google Workspace agreements.
